newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may cut deficit below 3% of GDP by 2005 - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan may cut deficit below 3% of GDP by 2005 - MOF.

text.p: Japan will likely be able to reduce its fiscal deficit to below three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2005, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday.

A government advisory panel recently submitted a report urging Japan to cut the fiscal deficit to less than three percent of GDP by 2005, with the initial step of holding spending below revenues in the next two to three years.
This spending would not include debt-servicing costs.
"If we continue on like this, we can surely achieve the goal," Mitsuzuka said.

He added that although the economy may stagger in the first half of the fiscal year starting April 1997, it will regain strength in the second half and will be able to achieve the official 1.9 percent economic forecast for the year.
